clue.text: Far too wet, so let's make this instead

definitions.text: Far too wet, so let's make this instead

indicators.note: making something else out of the same words tells us to rework the letters of the phrase before it

explanation.surface: Someone declares the weather far too wet for an outing and proposes a cosy alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FAR TOO WET are rearranged, signalled by 'make this instead'; the whole clue also describes the drink you brew when it is too wet to go out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot brewed for a couple is the cosy indoor treat you might make on a rainy day, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Cupid with a variety of rose

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters of the flower are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener names a new strain of rose after the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love is the counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: More fed in a liberated state

definitions.text: More fed in a liberated state

indicators.note: letters set loose from their order are free to fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Prisoners released from captivity find they are better nourished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a liberated state' tells you to set the letters of MORE FED loose and reorder them; the whole clue also describes the condition of being free.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty is the condition of a people or person no longer held captive.

clue.text: Read, it is said, as a warning to troublemakers

definitions.text: Read, it is said, as a warning to troublemakers

parts.words: Read, it is said, as a warning to troublemakers
parts.note: the old statute read aloud to an unruly crowd, ordering it to disperse; to read it now means to give a stern telling-off

explanation.surface: An official reads out a formal warning to a crowd of trouble-makers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1714 Act of Parliament was read to unlawful gatherings in Britain; the idiom 'read someone the ... act' survives as a severe reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the statute once read to dispersing mobs, now any stern reprimand.

clue.text: That which sounds a powerful unit

indicators.note: the word meaning 'that which' is only heard, and the answer is its sound-alike

parts.note: the relative pronoun what means that which, as in 'what I want'

explanation.surface: A riddling remark about a mighty military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the SI unit of power, one joule per second.

clue.text: Uncle's assessment 8 a pledge, perhaps

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, who puts a price on the item pledged; an uncle is also a family member

explanation.surface: A family member weighs up how much a promise is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The '8' is a scan misreading of 'of'. In British slang a pawnbroker is called 'uncle', and the pledge is the item pawned; an uncle is also kin, so his valuation is a kinsman's value.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means worth judged in comparison, and punningly the valuation a kinsman (the pawnbroker 'uncle') puts on a pawned item.

clue.text: Won't be long on the screen

explanation.surface: A cinema promises that a film will appear on screen soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means arriving soon, and is the stock caption on cinema trailers for forthcoming films.

clue.text: Nowhere near a means of checking

definitions.text: Nowhere near a means of checking

parts.note: something nowhere near is far off, distant
to check something is to restrain or govern it

explanation.surface: A description of a supervisory method that keeps its distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset lets you operate a device from a distance, governing it without being near it.

clue.text: A condition common in all spheres

definitions.text: A condition common in all spheres

parts.words: A condition common in all spheres
parts.note: spheres here are round balls, not fields of activity, and the condition they share is roundness

explanation.surface: A general remark about a state of affairs found in every walk of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spheres' looks like fields of life; read it as balls and the shared condition is roundness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means plumpness or roundness, which every ball has.

clue.text: Peter, I'm in a book and children love it

parts.note: Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the book receiving the I'm

parts.note: a tome is a large book
I'm contracted to its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone named Peter boasts of appearing in a children's favourite book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the contraction inside the big book, splitting it after its third letter; the surface's 'book' reads as Peter's story, but it is a tome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christmas stage show with slapstick and audience shouting is a family treat beloved by youngsters.

clue.text: Non-event at the races in Algeria

parts.note: nothing happening is nil, the letter O
what horses do at a race meeting, they ran

explanation.surface: A race meeting in North Africa where nothing happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O ran' reads as 'nothing ran', a race with no runners.
explanation.definitionFit: The port is the second city of that North African country.

clue.text: My job as banker at pontoon couldn't be better

parts.note: speaking of oneself, the first person I
in the card game pontoon the banker hands out the cards, that is deals

explanation.surface: A card player relishes taking the bank at pontoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for blackjack (twenty-one); the banker deals the cards, so the player says 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect is as good as it can be, the best possible.

clue.text: Recollect a little taste in Tuscany

indicators.note: re-collect read as gather back, so the words are taken back to front

parts.note: a sip is a small taste of a drink

explanation.surface: Someone remembers sampling a little wine in central Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollect' is read as collect again in reverse: A SIP turned round gives the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The city with the leaning tower lies in that region of Italy.

clue.text: Firm friend substantially resinous

definitions.note: the adjectival phrase stands for a noun, a substance that is resinous

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A loyal companion who is largely sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substantially resinous' means a substance that is resin, so the noun fits.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hard tropical tree resin used in varnishes.

clue.text: Tweedy mixture worn by many around Virginia

indicators.note: the word for many surrounds the state's abbreviation

parts.note: a lot means many
VA is the postal abbreviation of the US state

explanation.surface: Tweed garments are popular across a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a muted grey-green blend of colours typical of Scottish tweed.

clue.text: Identical apparel

explanation.surface: Clothing that looks the same on everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unvarying, the same throughout, and also the standard dress of a school or service.

clue.text: Speculation of 12 with the loss of a pound

annotationWithheld.why: Speculation of 12 with the loss of a pound: '12' is a cross-reference whose answer cannot be identified (12-across here is IDEAL, which gives no parse), so the wordplay cannot be shown
annotationWithheld.clue: Speculation of 12 with the loss of a pound

clue.text: I had red origins? Never

indicators.note: the letters are traced back to a different source order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A staunch conservative indignantly denies ever having been a socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins' signals rearranging I HAD RED; the whole clue is the stubborn denial such a person makes.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbending traditionalist would flatly refuse any suggestion of a left-wing past.

clue.text: Skilled assistant at the fish fishmonger's?

definitions.text: Skilled assistant at the fish fishmonger's?

parts.words: Skilled assistant at the fish fishmonger's?
parts.note: a hand is a worker and a dab is a flatfish, so a helper on the fish counter would be an expert

explanation.surface: An expert helper works behind a fish counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A dab is a small flatfish and a hand is a worker; the phrase means an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an expert, someone adept at a task.

clue.text: Where teatime meat is displayed in town…

parts.note: cha is slang for tea and T abbreviates time
ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: A town shop shows off cold cuts for the afternoon meal.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea, T is time; then HAM. The town is in Kent, England, home of the old naval dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a town on the Medway in Kent, England.

clue.text: Forthright with a Shaw heroine

parts.note: a forthright person is candid, frank

explanation.surface: A frank woman from a George Bernard Shaw play.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the title character of Shaw's 1894 play.

clue.text: … with duck if out late

indicators.note: letters that are out of place need to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the town scene: a duck dish served if the meal is late.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the clue before; 'out' tells you to rearrange LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small freshwater species of the bird.

clue.text: Old Japanese coin found in a noted Scottish resort

parts.note: Oban is a seaside town on the west coast of Scotland
given a note, here the musical note G

explanation.surface: An antique coin from Japan turns up in a famous Scottish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' looks like famous, but it supplies a musical note, G, added to the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a large oval gold piece of the Edo period.

clue.text: A strange piece of vegetation

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd bit of greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lily-like plant, such as cuckoo-pint.

clue.text: Gripping substitute

explanation.definitionFit: The bench tool clamps work in its jaws, and as a prefix the word means deputy, as in vice-president.

clue.text: Cotton fabric suitable for the garden

explanation.surface: A fine cloth ideal for outdoor use.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fine linen or cotton cloth and also a stretch of mown grass.

clue.text: Strictly moral partner, and how he conducts himself

definitions.text: Strictly moral partner, and how he conducts himself

parts.words: Strictly moral partner, and how he conducts himself
parts.note: a prudish, strait-laced man and the manner in which he behaves; the adverb describes that conduct

explanation.surface: A description of a spouse with rigid principles and his behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an adverb, so it is 'how he conducts himself': the strait-laced partner behaves in a severe, sternly moral manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes behaving with rigid, joyless moral strictness, like a seventeenth-century Protestant zealot.

clue.text: Protective covering that makes a plant die

indicators.note: the words are made into something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coating so toxic it kills any plant it touches.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a toxic coating once widely used to protect woodwork.
